papers.title: Representation of compounds for machine-learning prediction of physical properties
papers.abstract: The representations of a compound, called "descriptors" or "features", play an essential role in constructing a machine-learning model of its physical properties. In this study, we adopt a procedure for generating a systematic set of descriptors from simple elemental and structural representations. First it is applied to a large dataset composed of the cohesive energy for about 18000 compounds computed by density functional theory (DFT) calculation. As a result, we obtain a kernel ridge prediction model with a prediction error of 0.041 eV/atom, which is close to the "chemical accuracy" of 1 kcal/mol (0.043 eV/atom). The procedure is also applied to two smaller datasets, i.e., a dataset of the lattice thermal conductivity (LTC) for 110 compounds computed by DFT calculation and a dataset of the experimental melting temperature for 248 compounds. We examine the performance of the descriptor sets on the efficiency of Bayesian optimization in addition to the accuracy of the kernel ridge regression models. They exhibit good predictive performances.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注化合物物理性质的机器学习预测，与用户的方向（有限元代理建模、生物力学设计）无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses ML for materials property prediction from DFT data, not surrogate modeling for expensive FEA simulations, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_en.motivation: To develop systematic compound descriptors for accurate machine-learning prediction of physical properties.
summary_en.method: Descriptors are generated from elemental and structural representations and combined with kernel ridge regression for property prediction.
summary_en.result: Prediction error for cohesive energy reaches 0.041 eV/atom, approaching chemical accuracy.
summary_en.validation: Validated on large DFT-computed dataset of 18,000 compounds and smaller datasets for thermal conductivity and melting temperature.
